thread:
jamie: quick sync — we keep hitting ambiguity in gateway routing for model selection. current rules only do path prefix + query. need header overrides and alias pinning so product teams can opt into canaries without changing upstream clients.

sara: +1. can we have a precedent: route.match by path, header, and an optional route-level alias. e.g. `X-Model-Alias: chat-proxy-v2` or `?model_alias=`. Console should let us pin an alias to a route at 0/25/50/100% rollout.

mike: technical constraints to watch: model compatibility (kv-cache layout, tokenizer version, max_seq_len) — we can't fall back to a variant with incompatible KV format. need a compatibility tag matrix.

jamie: agreed. rough config idea:
```yaml
route: /api/chat/*
matchers:
  - type: prefix
    value: /api/chat
  - type: header
    name: X-Model-Alias
    precedence: high
overrides:
  alias_header: X-Model-Alias
  query_param: model_alias
default_alias: chat-latest
rollout:
  type: weighted
  variants:
    - alias: chat-latest
      weight: 90
    - alias: chat-canary-2026-03
      weight: 10
compatibility_constraints: [tokenizer:v2, kv_format:v2, max_seq_len:4096]
```

eva: console UX note — make alias pinning explicit: show what capabilities the alias supports and warn if pinning to an alias reduces throughput or requires dedicated nodes (e.g., quantized-int8 vs fp16). also surface estimated cost delta and latency impact before saving.

sara: telemetry: we should emit `routing.decision` events with fields: route_id, chosen_alias, reason (header|query|default|fallback), fallback_chain, chosen_model_version, latency_ms, token_count, cost_estimate. that'll let infra tie routing policy changes to SLO regressions.

mike: fallback policy specifics: prefer model with exact compatibility, then compatible-quantized variants, then last-resort serverless hosted small model. do not auto-fallback across major tokenizer mismatch. and log a high-severity alert when fallback alters output shape (e.g., different special tokens).

jamie: about quotas — when route pins to an alias that maps to Dedicated capacity, enforce route-level quotas and surface quota usage in the route dashboard. also provide an override header `X-Allow-Overquota` only for internal debug and gated by RBAC/audit.

eva: rollout UX: add a canary monitor that compares PDQ metrics (latency, perplexity on golden prompts, hallucination rate) between baseline and candidate. when metric delta > threshold, block promotion and notify owners.

sara: implementation note — keep config small and declarative. We should reuse model metadata service for capabilities instead of embedding full capability lists in route config. route config references alias IDs and the system resolves compatibility at deploy-time.

jamie: migration path: existing routes without alias support should default to `default_alias` and we add a two-week deprecation warn window if route behavior would change after enabling header overrides.

mike: security: header-based overrides must be sanitized and allowed only for trusted clients. otherwise a random client could force expensive models. validate token scopes in gateway.

deploy-bot: rollout started for `eng-platform/route-config` changes — cfg-2026-03-12T09:20Z (:rocket:)

jamie: next steps: mike + sara to sketch compatibility matrix prototype, eva to prototype console mockups (show alias capabilities + cost), i'll draft gateway spec. sync tomorrow 10am.
